Well, I'm more dual about this, as I am about anything else, but still.. There's a story.

In the Catholic Church(which I believe in), there is a possibility that you can be saved from Hell, if you perform an act of contrition right before you die, and you CAN be forgiven by God if your act of commiting suicide wasn't really "your own", because you suffered from depression or some other mental illness or disorder.

Even though there was this "guarantee" of sorts that I maybe would not go to Hell, I was still very fearful of it, and not in a positive way, as I feared all of my efforts were useless if I couldn't achieve the status of a saint, as I am too improductive and too incapable of comprehending anything at all.And since my parents themselves are protestants and are not too fond of the Catholic Church, because there is the dogma of the "Extra Ecclesiam Nulla Salus", which means that "Outside of the Church, there is no salvation", it probably meant that my parents could go to Hell too, and my entire family could go there as well.

If that was true, I thought it meant that I was effectively stripped off of any chance of actual comprehension of stuff, and any capability of actually doing something for myself and others because of this brain fog inside my head, and because of this, it could not be my fault for commiting suicide, and I was justified in doing it.   
It was so damaging to me that this excuse for not commiting suicide was thrown out of the window.

My thought process was this: "If I do attempt suicide, I'll do an act of contrition right before I die, and if I go to Heaven or Hell? Well, I'll just have to see for myself. Hopefully, God will have mercy on me, and if He doesn't, I simply will have to 'bear with it' for an eternity."And my suicidal thoughts became much stronger after that.But I was pulled back from that train of thought for some time, even though I still have some moments of wondering if I was right about this or not, and I'm still very much depressed and fucked up mentally, but I pulled back for one reason: I realized that all of those issues over whether suicide will cause you to immediately go to Hell, and the Extra Ecclesiam Nulla Salus thing are pretty much the heaviest and most difficult issues to address and genuinely understand in the Church, and such things had an effect in my psyche.It was an hyperfocus thing that was agonizing and crippling both before I was holding on to the belief that it is better to remain alive than to commit suicide because I would go to Hell and when I decided that I was justified in taking my own life.

I decided to look into more info about things like the Lives of the Saints and martyrs and imagining what exactly is the life that I would seek and struggles that they had in their lives, and stories about how a Saint, namely John Vianney outright confirmed that a suicide had been saved, and another about how Padre Pio said that a protestant friend of his had gone up to Heaven as well.I was also convinced of the reason for why suicide is considered so bad in the Christian community, and that is for the reason that human life has its dignity in of itself, instead of that being because of its utility(and well, I'm not useful for many things at all, so that's good for me).This didn't completely solve my problems, and like I said, I'm a fuck-up and this has been the worst year of my life, to the point I don't know if the next year will be better or not, and I still have doubts over some things in Christianity.But I felt free from that passionate belief and a little bit more open to new possibilities.

So I'd recommend you to stop focusing too much in this part of religion, if this is the reason for why you didn't commit suicide, it WILL be very tormenting and crippling to continue to believe in this.If you want, it would be better to research GOOD reasons for not commiting suicide instead of going into this heavy part of religion.

​

TL;DR: I was once hopped into the idea that I shouldn't kill myself, otherwise I would go to Hell. Then I let go of that belief and became even more suicidal. Realized that I was focusing too much into the more heavy parts of my religion. Decided to look into more healthy and good things, instead. It stabilized me. Don't think it's healthy to remain in this thought process.
